match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the broad set of business objectives in the brief, including meeting a social need and shareholder expectations; they cover narrower marketing, operations, financial and time-frame objectives from the NSW Business Studies course.

draft.title: Business objectives
card: A business objective is a goal the business sets to work towards. Objectives guide the decisions managers make.
Profit
making money after costs are paid. Market share is the business's portion of total sales in its market, and a business can aim to increase it.
Efficiency
using resources such as time, labour and materials with little waste. Effectiveness is how well the business achieves its objectives.
Social need and shareholders
a business may aim to meet a social need in the community. A listed company may aim to meet shareholder expectations, such as returns on their investment.
draft.remember: Objectives are the goals that guide a business, and a business can hold several at once.

a.q: A business reorganises its factory so it makes the same products using less material and fewer hours. Which objective is it pursuing?
a.why: Using fewer resources for the same output is improving efficiency. It is not market share, because nothing here is about taking a larger portion of sales.
a.clue: Focus on resources used for the same output.

b.q: Priya's phone repair shop in Ballarat cuts prices to win customers from rivals, and it expects its portion of local repairs to grow. Which objective is this?
b.why: Winning customers from rivals so its portion of local repairs grows is increasing market share. Profit may follow, but the aim described is a larger portion of sales, not lower resource use.
b.clue: What portion of the market does she want to grow?

problems.detail: The clue 'What portion of the market does she want to grow?' almost spells out 'market share', and the stem already says 'its portion of local repairs to grow', echoing the card's definition. A student can match the words without understanding the idea.

b.q: Priya's phone repair shop in Ballarat cuts its prices so that people stop using the other two repair shops in town. Which objective is this?
b.why: Drawing customers away from rivals means Priya's shop gains more of the town's total repair sales, which is increasing market share. It is not efficiency, because nothing here changes how much time, labour or materials each repair uses.
b.clue: Think about where her new customers come from.
